newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: Andean Pact to seek free-trade deal with Mercosur.
newsitem.headline: Andean Pact to seek free-trade deal with Mercosur.

text.p: The Andean Pact has agreed to seek a free-trade agreement with the Mercosur customs union, Venezuela's Foreign Minister Miguel Angel Burelli Rivas said Monday.
"We are all going to join, the whole Andean community," he told Reuters in the Bolivian city of Cochabamba, where the Rio Group of 14 Latin American nations is holding its 10th presidential summit.
Burelli said Andean Pact foreign ministers met earlier Monday in Cochabamba to discuss their plans, and the decision was taken after consulting with Mercosur nations.
"Yesterday it was just Venezuela that was going to join (Mercosur) first, but now it has been decided that we are all going to do it," he said.
The Andean Pact groups Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Bolivia, while Mercosur -- South America's biggest trade bloc -- includes Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay.
Chile has negotiated a free-trade agreement with Mercosur and Bolivia has also been negotiating a similar accord. Venezuela previously expressed interest in a pact as well.

Mercosur and Andean Pact presidents started to arrive Monday in Cochabamba, but Burelli declined to say whether they would make a formal announcement at the two-day summit, which officially starts Tuesday.
Burelli said that Mercosur will decide the framework within which the talks take place. "Mercosur will provide all the mechanics," he said.
